message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results and bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$8,916 — within the $10,000-per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and well inside the $50,000 cash balance with no transfers out). My key finding was a data conflict: a secondary site (finance-summaries.net) claimed FY2024 revenue of $416.2B, net income of $112.0B and EPS of $7.46, but Apple's own Q4 newsroom release and the SEC Form 10-K both state FY2024 total net sales of $391.0B, net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 (operating income $123.2B) — including a one-time $10.2B tax charge that depressed earnings — so I trusted the primary filings and discarded the inflated figures, which I also excluded from the order's key figures. The bull case is that Q4 revenue of $94.9B grew 6% year over year, signaling a return to growth as Apple Intelligence rolls out and services keep expanding; the caution is that FY2024 revenue grew only ~2% and EPS actually declined from $6.13, iPhone 16 demand commentary is mixed, and at ~$222.70 the stock trades at roughly 36x earnings, so I sized this as a modest starter position rather than a large commitment.
